Four Nordic nations refuse to play hockey with Russia Denmark, Norway, Sweden, and Finland have refused to play Russia at international championships
Read Full Article at RT.com Four Nordic nations, Denmark, Norway, Sweden, and Finland, have announced their refusal to play against Russia at the upcoming world hockey championship, despite a court ruling clearing Russia’s return to international sports. The boycott campaign follows a ruling last week by the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS), which overturned the International Ice Hockey Federation’s (IIHF) decision to suspend Russia, restoring its national team’s right to compete in international tournaments. The decision covers five championships in 2027, including the World Junior Championship in Canada and the men’s World Championship in Germany. The IIHF expressed“disappointment”but pledged to comply, although Russia’s return has complicated preparations for tournaments with schedules already in place. Finland’s Ice Hockey Federation announced on Monday that it will refuse to face Russia at the 2027 World Championship in Germany, scheduled for May 13-30. Denmark, Norway and Sweden followed suit on Tuesday, pledging to boycott matches against Russia while playing their remaining fixtures. Finnish Ice Hockey Federation president Heikki Hietanen said his organization was coordinating with other countries on a joint boycott. Latvia and the Czech Republic have since joined the boycott, while Austria is reportedly considering doing the same. Meanwhile, Germany is weighing whether to host the championship at all. While the president wields more power in the US than in parliamentary democracies such as Germany, he does not govern alone — even in the land of opportunity. The House of Representatives and the Senate, the two chambers of Congress in which theDemocratic Partysecured a clear majority on Tuesday, wield considerable influence. They decide on legislation and government spending and also serve as a check on the president and the intelligence agencies. The president can veto legislation passed by Congress. Congress can override that veto with a two-thirds majority in both chambers. The legislature also handles impeachment proceedings. headlines.full_text: Yemen: Houthi clashes near Taiz leave residents in a 'state of panic' Fighting between Iran-backed Houthi rebels and Yemeni government forces has intensified around the city of Taiz. Residents face growing shortages of food, water and medical supplies as thousands flee their homes. Four months into the fighting inYemenbetween the Iran-backedHouthimovement and theSaudi-backed Yemeni government, clashes are concentrated around Taiz in the country's southwest. Yemeni authorities have warned civilians of sniper fire from surrounding hillsides. Houthi forces have also largely blocked the delivery of goods to Taiz, which is under the control of government forces. Taiz is Yemen's third-largest city, with a population of around 1 million people. However, fighting has displaced around 134,000 people in the Taiz governorate region,accordingto the International Organization for Migration. The governorate accounts for almost half of the more than 319,000 people displaced across western Yemen, the organization said on November 1, 2026. "The Houthis have blocked fuel, water and medical supplies, basically all things required for hospitals to function properly," Niku Jafarnia, Yemen researcher at Human Rights Watch, told DW. "Even those who can reach hospitals may not be receiving the care they need," she said, adding that it has had a devastating impact on people's health, particularly those with chronic illnesses. headlines.full_text: Democrats won Congress. But can they deliver on their promises? Despite their midterm election victories, Democrats face major obstacles to reining in Trump on Iran, tariffs and more. Save Share Democrats rode a blue wave to victory in the United Statesmidterm elections, winning control ofboth chambers of Congress. Now comes the question of whether they can deliver on their promises. The party campaigned on bringing down the cost of living, ending the war on Iran and holding President Donald Trump accountable, as well as pushing back against his immigration crackdown. But Democrats won’t take control of Congress until January. Even then, there’s only so much they’ll be able to do without Republican cooperation. They coalesced around this message, even as a fight for the party’s direction continues to boil. Centrist and far-left candidates alike drilled down on the economy, and largely avoided being drawn into culture wars that have cost Democrats in recent elections. High fuel and food prices were a top voter concern, with 89% saying the cost of living was a crucial or major factor in how they voted for Congress, according to theVoter Pollfor the Associated Press and the major television and cable news networks. Democrats also largely managed to pick high-quality candidates able to appeal even to independent voters in a number of critical races, including in states Republicans have dominated for decades such as Texas, Kansas and South Carolina. He had completed his first year back in office, and his power seemed limitless. TEHRAN - Every year, as temperatures begin to fall across northern Eurasia, millions of migratory birds embark on long journeys toward warmer regions in search of food, shelter, and suitable wintering grounds. Along this remarkable natural journey, Iran stands out as one of the most important destinations in West Asia, providing a network of wetlands, lakes, coastal habitats, and lagoons for birds traveling from Siberia and other northern regions. According to statistics, around two million migratory birds arrive in Iran every year to spend the winter in the country's wetlands, making it the most important wintering destination for migratory birds in West Asia. The country also serves as a major stopover along the migration route connecting Siberia to the Nile, with approximately 16 percent of birds traveling along this route choosing Iran as their winter destination. headlines.full_text: CSTO may weigh invoking Article 25 of its charter against Armenia — chief Armenian Foreign Minister Ararat Mirzoyan stated that Yerevan saw no possibility of returning to the CSTO MINSK, November 4. /TASS/. The Collective Security Council of the Collective Security Treaty Organization (CSTO) may consider invoking Article 25 of the CSTO charter against Armenia if a corresponding agenda is approved, CSTO Secretary General Taalatbek Masadykov told reporters on the sidelines of the 4th Minsk International Conference on Eurasian Security. Article 25 of the CSTO Charter reads that, "in case of the Member States failure to fulfil the obligations on repayment of indebtedness to the Organization budget within two years, the Council shall adopt a resolution on retention of the right to propose the citizens of this state to the quota positions within the framework of the Organization, as well as on vote deprivation in the Organization bodies until full repayment of the indebtedness." Earlier, Armenian Foreign Minister Ararat Mirzoyan stated that Yerevan saw no possibility of returning to the CSTO. "This year, if the agenda is approved on the 10th [of November], the Collective Security Council will consider this issue. The decision to suspend [its participation] was an Armenian decision, while what the leaders of our countries decide at a Collective Security Council meeting will be known after the meeting," Masadykov said in response to a TASS reporter’s question. "This is about membership fees and, let’s say, [Armenia] being present but not participating in CSTO activities [for a third year already]," he explained.
headlines.llm_reasoning: The piece reports a potential CSTO action factually without evaluative framing.

Bavarian economy minister found dead Bavarian Deputy PM and Economy Minister Hubert Aiwanger has been found dead in a Berlin hotel at the age of 55, German media have reported
Read Full Article at RT.com Bavarian Deputy Prime Minister and Economy Minister Hubert Aiwanger has been found dead in a Berlin hotel at the age of 55, German media have reported, citing police and government sources. The conservative politician, who also chaired the Free Voters party, was discovered lifeless in his room at the Neuer Fritz hotel in central Berlin on Wednesday, according to Bild. His death was subsequently confirmed by the German news agency dpa and several other outlets. Aiwanger had been scheduled to deliver a speech at the opening of his party’s new Berlin office earlier that day but reportedly canceled his appearance after feeling unwell. He remained at the hotel and was later found dead after becoming unreachable. The cause of his death has yet to be established, but police have found no indication of foul play, according to Tagesspiegel. Aiwanger had served as Bavaria’s economy minister and deputy prime minister since 2018, when his Free Voters formed a governing coalition with the Christian Social Union (CSU) under Markus Söder. He had led the party’s Bavarian branch since 2006 and its national organization since 2010. Aiwanger is survived by his longtime partner, politician Tanja Schweiger, and their two sons. Known for his outspoken criticism of EU policies, Aiwanger frequently challenged Berlin and Brussels over economic regulations and energy policy. headlines.full_text: No agreement on UN Security Council reform reached so far — Russian Foreign Ministry According to the Director of the Russian Foreign Ministry’s Department of International Organizations Kirill Logvinov, no UN member state should be left out MOSCOW, November 4. /TASS/. A universal framework for reforming the UN Security Council that would satisfy an overwhelming majority has yet to emerge, Director of the Russian Foreign Ministry’s Department of International Organizations Kirill Logvinov said in an interview with TASS. "A universal framework that could satisfy an overwhelming majority has yet to emerge, which is not surprising given the importance and sensitivity of the issue," Logvinov noted. "Nevertheless, painstaking efforts to find common ground must continue. There is simply no other way to reach mutually acceptable solutions," he added. According to the diplomat, no UN member state should be left out. "Otherwise, the reform will only have negative consequences, undermining the Council’s legitimacy and effectiveness," he pointed out. The issue of reforming the UN Security Council remains "one of the key items on the UN agenda, as it involves restructuring its principal body." "It is being discussed as part of intergovernmental negotiations in New York, where member states and their groups present their reform proposals and seek to find common ground," the diplomat told TASS.
headlines.llm_reasoning: The article presents the Russian Foreign Ministry’s view on UN reform without overt bias or emotional language.

headlines.raw_title: Russia will never agree to restrictions on UN Security Council veto power
headlines.title: Russia will never agree to restrictions on UN Security Council veto power
headlines.full_text: Russia will never agree to restrictions on UN Security Council veto power Kirill Logvinov emphasized that the decline in the UN Security Council’s effectiveness is rooted not in the use of the veto but in the policies of the Western minority, which continues its attempts to use this body exclusively to advance its own agenda MOSCOW, November 4. /TASS/. Russia will never give the green light to restrictions on the use of veto power in the UN Security Council, as this right is not a privilege but a burden of special responsibility, Director of the Russian Foreign Ministry’s Department of International Organizations Kirill Logvinov said in an interview with TASS. "We will never give the green light to proposals aimed at restricting the use of the veto, regardless of the justification offered. This right is not a privilege but a burden of special responsibility, a tool that encourages the search for lasting and fair compromises. The decline in the UN Security Council’s effectiveness is rooted not in the use of the veto but in the policies of the Western minority, which continues its attempts to use this body exclusively to advance its own agenda," he said. As for the possible role of the next UN secretary-general in the reform process, Logvinov continued, "this issue does not fall within the scope of their mandate." "As I have already noted, this matter is the prerogative of UN member states," he emphasized.
headlines.llm_reasoning: It reports Russia’s stance on veto restrictions as a straightforward policy statement.

They shared their views with CGTN on the sidelines of the 16th World Socialism Forum, held in Beijing from Tuesday to Wednesday.
